elements.problem: All parts encoded: temperature >= 38 °C OR body pain (Generalized aches and pains), painful lump (Breast lump AND Pain of breast), breast abscess likely as probable, urgent attention as Urgent via active_condition. 'Which may be fluctuant' is permissive wording, not a criterion, so leaving it out is right. Minor points: the painful lump is split into two independent findings, so pain in one breast and a lump in the other still fires; the presenting complaint is implicit rather than an explicit (and <complaint> ...) wrapper, which the briefing's active_condition pattern allows.

rule_level_problems.problem: The page reaches 'mastalgia likely' only after 'If none of [the warning signs] above, continue'. The rule doesn't check for or exclude any warning sign: skin changes, irregular fixed lump, nipple discharge, axillary lump, age/family-history combinations. A patient with breast pain plus a red-flag combination could still be labelled probable mastalgia, provided 'Breast normal' is recorded, which partly mitigates this.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable breast abscess / Diagnose probable mastitis associated with lactation
rule_level_problems.problem: These overlap. A breastfeeding patient with fever or body pain and a painful lump gets both probable abscess and probable mastitis. The page sends such a patient to the red box (abscess) before the non-urgent mastitis branch, but the mastitis rule doesn't exclude a lump. The page's 'with or without lump' makes this defensible, so it is a design note, not an error.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable breast engorgement / Diagnose probable blocked milk duct
rule_level_problems.problem: The No branch requires a recorded temperature < 38 °C. If temperature isn't measured, neither diagnosis fires, even though the page's No branch is just 'no fever or body pain'.

The due_to 'Breast finding' is not a recorded common symptom or warning sign. 'Maternal breastfeeding' is a descendant of Breast finding (is_a YES), so the check task also triggers on breastfeeding alone. The check list has no warning-sign items (see the mastalgia note). Every check_for item is consumed by some rule.

summary: The red box (urgent probable breast abscess) and the breastfeeding branch (mastitis vs engorgement/blocked duct on temperature >= 38 °C or body pain) are encoded correctly, with valid SNOMED concepts and correct Yes/No negation. The most consequential gap: the warning-sign screen ('if none of above, continue') isn't encoded, so probable mastalgia isn't gated on the absence of red flags. Smaller issues: abscess and mastitis overlap, and engorgement/blocked duct depend on a recorded temperature.
